jp: 台所[だいどころ]から{何[なに]か|ko-ka}いい匂[にお]いがします。
en: Something smells good from the kitchen.
why: An unspecified something that is perceived is 何か; 何も needs a negative.

jp: 夕食[ゆうしょく]の前[まえ]に、{何[なに]か|ko-ka}手伝[てつだ]うことはある？
en: Is there anything I can help with before dinner?
why: A question offering unspecified help asks 何か, 'something or anything'.

jp: 祖母[そぼ]の部屋[へや]で{何[なに]か|ko-ka}落[お]ちる音[おと]がしました。
en: I heard something fall in Grandma's room.
why: The thing that fell is unknown and unspecified, so it is 何か.

jp: 朝[あさ]は、{何[なに]か|ko-ka}軽[かる]いものを食[た]べてから出[で]かけます。
en: In the morning I eat something light before going out.
why: One unspecified light item that I eat is 何か.

jp: 父[ちち]は、寝[ね]る前[まえ]に{何[なに]か|ko-ka}飲[の]む習慣[しゅうかん]があります。
en: My father has a habit of drinking something before bed.
why: An unspecified drink in an affirmative statement is 何か.

jp: 玄関[げんかん]のベルが鳴[な]りました。{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}来[き]たようです。
en: The doorbell rang. Someone seems to have come.
why: An unidentified person who exists is 誰か; 誰も would need a negative.

jp: 妹[いもうと]は、電話[でんわ]で{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}と楽[たの]しそうに話[はな]しています。
en: My younger sister is talking happily with someone on the phone.
why: The person is unknown to the speaker, so it is 誰か (with と outside the slot).

jp: 洗濯物[せんたくもの]が取[と]り込[こ]んであります。{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}がやってくれたようです。
en: The laundry has been brought in. Someone seems to have done it for me.
why: An unidentified person did it, so it is 誰か, followed by the subject marker が.

jp: 夜中[よなか]に、{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}が台所[だいどころ]を歩[ある]いている音[おと]がしました。
en: In the middle of the night I heard someone walking around in the kitchen.
why: A person I could not identify is 誰か; 誰も cannot go with a positive statement.

jp: 子[こ]どもが熱[ねつ]を出[だ]しました。{誰[だれ]か|ko-ka}、病院[びょういん]まで車[くるま]で送[おく]ってくれませんか。
en: My child has a fever. Could someone drive us to the hospital?
why: The speaker asks an unspecified person for help, so it is 誰か, 'someone'.

jp: 今度[こんど]の連休[れんきゅう]は、家族[かぞく]で{どこか|ko-ka}涼[すず]しいところへ行[い]きたいね。
en: Over the next long weekend I'd like to go somewhere cool with the family.
why: An unspecified destination in a wish is どこか.

jp: 子[こ]どもの靴下[くつした]が{どこか|ko-ka}に行[い]ってしまいました。
en: The child's socks have gone off somewhere.
why: The socks are somewhere unknown, so it is どこか, followed by に.

jp: 家[いえ]の中[なか]の{どこか|ko-ka}に、古[ふる]いアルバムがあるはずです。
en: Somewhere in the house there should be an old album.
why: An unspecified place where something should be is どこか.

jp: 今夜[こんや]の夕食[ゆうしょく]は、{どこか|ko-ka}外[そと]で食[た]べませんか。
en: Shall we eat dinner somewhere out tonight?
why: An unspecified place proposed for an invitation is どこか.

jp: 子[こ]どもたちが大[おお]きくなったら、{いつか|ko-ka}家族[かぞく]で外国[がいこく]に住[す]んでみたいです。
en: Someday, when the children are older, I'd like to try living abroad as a family.
why: A vague point in the future ('someday') is いつか; いつも would mean always.

jp: 祖父[そふ]は、{いつか|ko-ka}この家[いえ]を建[た]て直[なお]したいと言[い]っていました。
en: Grandfather used to say he wanted to rebuild this house someday.
why: An unspecified future time for a hope is いつか.

jp: 引[ひ]っ越[こ]しが終[お]わったら、{いつか|ko-ka}みんなで庭[にわ]でバーベキューをしましょう。
en: Once the move is over, let's have a barbecue in the garden together sometime.
why: A loosely proposed future time with no date is いつか.

jp: 兄[あに]の夢[ゆめ]は、{いつか|ko-ka}自分[じぶん]の家[いえ]を建[た]てることです。
en: My brother's dream is to build his own house someday.
why: A dream with no fixed date is placed at some unspecified time, いつか.
